name: Reentrancy on state-changing external call
requires: an external call (native value, token transfer, hook, or arbitrary target) reachable by an unprivileged caller
state written after that call, or accounting derived from a live balance the call can change
value present at the fork block that the reentry can reach
foundry with a fork RPC at the deployment block

false_positives: A reentrancy guard is present under a different name (lock, entered, a ReentrancyGuard base) and was not read
The external call is after the state write; only the grep ordering suggested otherwise
Reentry can only spend the attacker's own already-credited balance
The contract holds no value at the fork block, so the primitive has no consequence today
transfer() or send() with the 2300 gas stipend, which prevents a meaningful callback
The reentry reverts and the whole transaction reverts: griefing or self-DoS, not extraction
A staticcall into an attacker contract, which cannot mutate storage and is an oracle question instead
Cross-function claims where the two functions do not actually share the written slot
poc_must_show: attacker balance delta within one transaction or one atomic bundle, measured before and after
a control run with reentry disabled, showing the delta is attributable to the reentry and not to normal flow
the protocol or victim balance losing a corresponding amount, so the profit has a source
the call trace: outer entry, external call, inner entry, return, outer continues on stale state
no privileged role used, and capital in not greater than capital out
impact_bar: Reportable when an unprivileged account extracts value it did not deposit, or permanently locks funds a legitimate user could otherwise withdraw, with the amount quantified. Informational for gas-only griefing, self-DoS, or reentry requiring an already-privileged role.
